text: To be yourself requires extraordinary intelligence. You are blessed with that intelligence…
note: Goodreads/Wikiquote file it under Mystique; some aggregators attach it to No Way Out; inner-quest.org shows it as a talk transcript.

text: To realize that there is no enlightenment at all is enlightenment.
note: Followed by Q: "So there is enlightenment!" — UG: "If you want to call it that." Wikisource places it in Part Four; kwize says Part Three.

text: If you want to call it that.
note: UG's reply to the questioner's "So there is enlightenment!" after the line above.

text: Enlightenment (if there is any such thing as enlightenment) is not an experience at all.
Unquestioned action is morality.
note: Part of the Q&A passage beginning "What is morality? It is not the following of enjoined [rules]…". Most sites credit Mystique; one Goodreads listing credits Mind Is a Myth.

text: What is morality? It is not the following of enjoined…
note: The passage also says questioning one's actions is destroying the expression of life, and describes a man who lets life act without the protective movement of thought (paraphrased continuation).

text: …discovered that there is no such thing as enlightenment at all…
note: Continuation paraphrased: so the question of whether a particular person is enlightened does not arise.

text: there is no self to realize
note: Quotlr renders the longer version in paraphrase: the realization that there is no self to realize comes as a shattering blow, hits like a thunderbolt.

text: a bunch of exploiters, thriving on the gullibility of the people
note: On gurus and claimants to enlightenment.

text: …has no copyright. You are free to reproduce, distribute, interpret, misinterpret, distort, garble, do what you like…
note: The opening copyright-release statement, in place of a copyright notice; Wikiquote notes it recurs in several publications of his conversations.

text: …nature had been allowed to go on in its own way, everybody would have become a unique flower.
I call these events a calamity because from the point of view of one who thinks this is something fantastic, blissful, full of love, ecstasy and all that kind of a thing, this is physical torture.
Not a calamity to me but to those who have an image that something marvelous is going to happen.
This state is a physical condition of your being. It is not some kind of psychological mutation.
The natural state is acausal: it just happens.
note: Also quoted in publisher copy.

text: The things that had astonished me that week had become permanent fixtures.
By 1961 my money was finished…
note: Biographical passage; the summary also gives the fragment "…a tremendous upheaval…" which he later called the calamity, in his forty-ninth year (paraphrase).

text: …a tremendous upheaval…
note: Describing the events of 1967 he later called the calamity.

text: is like a nuclear explosion
note: On entering the natural state; quoted in the Simon & Schuster description.

text: The search ends with the realization that there is no such thing as enlightenment.
note: azquotes attributes to Mystique; Wikiquote places the related "search … choking me" passage under Mind is a Myth.

text: There is no power outside of man. Man has created God out of fear. So the problem is fear and not God.
note: hindu-blog carries the middle sentence alone; praveennv cites a Mind Is a Myth p.31 variant "it is the mind that has created God out of fear".

text: We don't want to be free from fear. All that we want to do is to play games with it and talk about freeing ourselves from fear.
If anyone thinks he can help you, he will inevitably mislead you…
note: Continuation paraphrased: and the less phony, the more powerful and enlightened he seems, the more misery and mischief he will create for you.

text: There is no such thing as experience here. You seem…
We are not created for any grander purpose than the…
Nature is interested in only two things--to survive and to…
one can do nothing to attain the natural state. In fact, any movement towards it separates one from it.
note: Editor's or publisher's words (Rodney Arms introduction / book description), NOT UG's own sentence.

text: Thought can never capture the movement of life, it is much too slow. It is like lightning and thunder. They occur simultaneously, but sound, traveling slower than light, reaches you later, creating the illusion of two separate events.
chapter: Ch. 3 Not Knowing Is Your Natural State
note: quotepark/azquotes place it in Ch.3; Wikisource shows it near a Chapter IV heading. Top quote on the Goodreads work page.

text: It (thinking) does not put an end to sorrow.
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything
note: Goodreads version omits the parenthesis.

text: Your thinking endlessly about being free from sorrow is only more material for sorrow.
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything

text: Sorrow is there for you as long as you think. There is actually no sorrow there to be free from.
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything

text: Only if you reject all the other paths can you discover your own path.
note: inner-quest.org has a variant "respect all the other paths" (likely error).

text: If you have the courage to touch life for the first time, you will never know what hit you. Everything man has thought, felt and experienced is gone, and nothing is put in its place.
chapter: Ch. 4 There Is Nothing To Understand
note: praveennv blog misprints "taught" for "thought".

text: It is the ones who believe in God, who preach peace and talk of love, who have created the human jungle. Compared to man…
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything
note: Continuation paraphrased: the so-called civilized man kills for ideals and beliefs, while animals kill only for survival.

text: There is no such thing as truth. The only thing that is actually there is your "logically" ascertained premise, which you call "truth."
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything

text: no qualitative change in man's thinking
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything
note: Near-verbatim fragment; the passage continues that the only change is "our ability to destroy our neighbor and his property."

text: our ability to destroy our neighbor and his property.
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything
note: The only change in man's thinking, in the passage above.

text: There is no such thing as spiritual or psychological enlightenment because there is no such thing as spirit or psyche at all.
note: Some reprints omit "at all". Followed by the "search itself which has been choking me" line.

text: I have had to search and it is the search itself which has been choking me and keeping me out of my natural state.
God or Enlightenment is the ultimate pleasure, uninterrupted happiness. No such thing exists.
note: Goodreads lists under Mind Is a Myth and No Way Out; Wikisource also has it in Thought is Your Enemy.

text: I am not anti-rational, just unrational. You may infer a rational meaning in what I say or do, but it is your doing,…
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything
note: Book not confirmed by search; usually Mind is a Myth Ch.1. Elsewhere also filed under No Way Out ch.1 essay title.

text: Nature is busy creating absolutely unique individuals, whereas culture has invented a single mold to which all must conform. It is grotesque.
note: Fragment on quotefancy ends at "conform"; "It is grotesque." confirmed by summary. Goodreads also lists it under The Courage to Stand Alone.

text: Food, clothing and shelter — these are the basic needs. Beyond that, if you…
note: Book not confirmed by search.

text: [damn fool passage, paraphrase only]
note: quotepark labels it Ch.4 but notes it is quoted in Terry Newland's Introduction (Newland quoting UG). Text not recovered.

text: Both the inner and outer worlds proceed from a point of thought; everything experienced is born out of thought, so experience is an illusion.
note: Paraphrase from kwize.

text: Tradition is a burden people cling to; it has to fall away on its own.
note: Paraphrase from kwize. Related verbatim fragment: "Your traditions are choking you."

text: Your traditions are choking you.
Nobody knows anything about life.
note: Paraphrase from the Goodreads author page.

text: Society is the human jungle; it would be much easier to survive in nature's jungle.
note: Paraphrase from quotepark/libquotes; "the human jungle" is verbatim.

text: Don't follow me, I'm lost.
The demand to be prepared for all future actions and all situations is the cause of our problems. Every situation is so different…
note: Wikisource text reads "actions and situations"; quote sites read "actions and all situations". Context: we don't know what we would do in a given situation.

text: Society or culture or whatever you might want to call it, has created us all solely and wholly for the purpose of maintaining its continuity and status quo.
chapter: Ch. II Throw Away Your Crutches
note: libquotes = Ch.II Throw Away Your Crutches; azquotes = Ch.III The Robot Is Dreaming.

text: Thought has interfered and trying to suppress, control, and moralize about desire, to the detriment of mankind.
note: Context: desire is a bodily, natural matter.

text: Our experience of our own body depends on thought, and thought is memory.
note: Paraphrase from Goodreads.

text: There is no such thing as your mind or my mind; a separate individual mind is an illusion; thought is a protective mechanism.
note: Paraphrase from Goodreads / holybooks summary.

text: transformation, moksha, and all that stuff are just variations of the same theme: permanent happiness
note: Also in No Way Out ch.1 essay on the WELL. Paraphrased continuation: the body cannot sustain that kind of pleasure.

text: The fixed "I" as a reference point; the courage needed to drop one's conditioning; rejecting what others offer is the real task.
note: Paraphrase of the remembering-ug "Passages from Thought is Your Enemy" posts.

text: …everything you stand for, believe in, experience and aspire to is the result of thought. And thought is destructive because it is nothing more than a protective mechanism.
note: Book not given by libquotes; commonly Thought is Your Enemy. quotefancy variant: thought is "nothing more than a protective mechanism, programmed to protect its own interests at all costs".

text: nothing more than a protective mechanism, programmed to protect its own interests at all costs
note: quotefancy variant of the thought-as-protective-mechanism line.

text: everything you are doing to be at peace with yourself is what is destroying the peace that is already there.
note: Book not given by libquotes.

text: …the constant use of thought to give continuity to your separate self.
note: Book not given by quotefancy.

text: the fear of losing what we have and what we know
note: Given as the cause of our problems; book not given by quotefancy. The full sentence is filed under No Way Out on Goodreads.

text: You can have the courage to climb the mountain, swim the lakes, go on a raft to the other side of the Atlantic or Pacific. … The courage to be on your own, to stand on your two solid feet, is something which cannot be given by somebody. You cannot free yourself of that burden by trying to develop that courage. If you are freed from the entire burden of the entire past of mankind, then what is left there is the courage.
You think when you don't want to do anything. Thinking is a poor alternative to acting. Your thinking is consuming all your energy. Act, don't think!
note: Recorded by Mahesh Bhatt. Wikiquote warns Bhatt's own observation "You are what you do, not what you say you want to do" is often wrongly merged into this quote.

text: A real guru, if there is one, frees you from himself.
note: Wikiquote Talk page, unsourced.

text: I still maintain that it is not love, compassion, humanism, or brotherly sentiments that will save mankind. No, not at…
note: Goodreads lists under No Way Out; paraphrased continuation: the sheer terror of extinction may do more to save humanity than love or humanism.

text: The plain fact is that if you don't have a problem, you create one.
your teacher must go, it doesn't matter who the teacher is
note: hindu-blog collection, no book given.

text: the demand for permanence-permanent relationships, permanent happiness, and permanent bliss-in any field and in any area of human existence is the cause of human misery
note: hindu-blog collection, no book given.

text: blind acceptance of authority, all second-hand stuff
note: On beliefs; hindu-blog collection, no book given.

text: basically violent, because thought is violent
note: On human nature; hindu-blog collection, no book given.

text: Charity is a way for the comfortable to keep the have-nots from rebelling and to ease their own guilt.
note: Paraphrase from quotlr.
